newsitem.title: USA: American Telecasting swap letter expires.
newsitem.headline: American Telecasting swap letter expires.

text.p: American Telecasting Inc said on Monday its letter of intent with CS Wireless Systems Inc to exchange certain wireless cable assets had expired.

American Telecasting said in a statement that under the terms of the letter, the company was to have swapped the wireless cable markets of Louisville, Ky.; Little Rock, Ark.; Oklahoma City; and Wichita, Kan., with CS Wireless.
In exchange, American Telecasting would have received the wireless cable markets of Minneapolis; Bakersfield, Calif.; and Stockton/Modesto, Calif., plus about $5.5 million in cash.
Robert D. Hostetler, American Telecasting's president and chief executive, said, "Although this letter of intent has expired, we will continue to seek transactions that rationalize our MDS assets."
American Telecasting Inc operates wireless cable television systems throughout the United States, serving about 178,100 subscribers in 38 markets.
